gloss: one's own book; one's own written work

definitions.gloss: one's own book; one's own publication; a book one has written
definitions.explanation: A book or written work authored by the person being discussed. Used when referring to someone's own published writing, especially in literary, academic, or media contexts.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}は{自著|じちょ}を{紹介|しょうかい}した。
examples.english: The professor introduced their own book.

examples.japanese: {自著|じちょ}にサインをして{読者|どくしゃ}に{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: They signed their own book and handed it to the reader.

examples.japanese: その{作家|さっか}は{自著|じちょ}の{中|なか}で{自分|じぶん}の{体験|たいけん}を{詳|くわ}しく{語|かた}っている。
examples.english: That author talks in detail about their own experiences in their book.

notes:
A compound of {自|じ} (self) and {著|ちょ} (written work, publication). Specifically refers to a book or publication that one has personally authored, as opposed to books by others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自著|じちょ}を{出版|しゅっぱん}する: to publish one's own book
- {自著|じちょ}を{紹介|しょうかい}する: to introduce one's own book
- {自著|じちょ}にサインする: to sign one's own book
- {自著|じちょ}の{中|なか}で: in one's own book

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {著書|ちょしょ}: written work, book — can refer to anyone's published book; {自著|じちょ} specifically means the speaker's or subject's own book
- {著作|ちょさく}: literary work, writing — broader term that includes any kind of authored content, not just books
- {拙著|せっちょ}: my humble work — a modest way to refer to one's own book; uses the self-deprecating prefix {拙|せつ}

REGISTER:
Formal. Commonly appears in interviews, book reviews, academic introductions, and literary discussion. In casual conversation, people would more naturally say {自分|じぶん}の{本|ほん} (my own book).
